p212.original: In 2020, more than 20 million people could collect unemployment insurance benefits to replace some of their salaries. Federal fiscal policies include discretionary fiscal policy, when the government passes a new law that explicitly changes tax or spending levels. The 2020 stimulus checks and increases in state and local government aid are an example. Changes in tax and spending levels can also occur automatically, due to automatic stabilizers, such as unemployment insurance and food stamps, which are programs that are already laws that stimulate aggregate demand in a recession and hold down aggregate demand in a potentially inflationary boom.
p212.zh: 2020年,超过2000万人可以领取失业保险金,以取代部分工资.联邦财政政策包括酌情制定财政政策,当政府通过一部明确改变税收或支出水平的新法律时。2020年刺激措施的检查以及州和地方政府援助的增加就是一个例子。税收和支出水平的改变也可能自动发生,因为自动稳定器,如失业保险和食品券,这些方案已经是刺激衰退中总需求的法律,并且在潜在的通货膨胀暴涨时抑制总需求。

p214.original: Consider first the situation where aggregate demand has risen sharply, causing the equilibrium to occur at a level of output above potential GDP. This situation will increase inflationary pressure in the economy. The policy prescription in this setting would be a dose of contractionary fiscal policy, implemented through some combination of higher taxes and lower spending. To some extent, both changes happen automatically. On the tax side, a rise in aggregate demand means that workers and firms throughout the economy earn more. Because taxes are based on personal income and corporate profits, a rise in aggregate demand automatically increases tax payments. On the spending side, stronger aggregate demand typically means lower unemployment and fewer layoffs, and so there is less need for government spending on unemployment benefits, welfare, Medicaid, and other programs in the social safety net.
p214.zh: 首先考虑总需求急剧上升的情况,这种平衡表现在产出水平高于潜在国内生产总值的水平上。 这种情况将增加经济的通货膨胀压力。 这种情况下的政策处方将是某种收缩性财政政策,通过提高税收和降低支出的某种组合加以实施。在某种程度上,两种变化都是自动发生的. 在税收方面,总需求的增加意味着整个经济的工人和公司赚取更多的收入。 由于税收是以个人收入和公司利润为基础的,总需求的上升会自动增加纳税额. 在支出方面,总需求增加通常意味着失业率降低,裁员减少,因此政府在失业福利、福利、医疗补助和社会安全网中的其他方案方面的支出需求减少。

p215.original: The process works in reverse, too. If aggregate demand were to fall sharply so that a recession occurs, then the prescription would be for expansionary fiscal policy—some mix of tax cuts and spending increases. The lower level of aggregate demand and higher unemployment will tend to pull down personal incomes and corporate profits, an effect that will reduce the amount of taxes owed automatically. Higher unemployment and a weaker economy should lead to increased government spending on unemployment benefits, welfare, and other similar domestic programs. In 2009, the stimulus package included an extension in the time allowed to collect unemployment insurance. In addition, the automatic stabilizers react to a weakening of aggregate demand with expansionary fiscal policy and react to a strengthening of aggregate demand with contractionary fiscal policy, just as the AD/AS analysis suggests.
p215.zh: 这一过程也以反向方式运作。 如果总需求急剧下降,从而出现衰退,那么,处方将是扩张性财政政策——减税和增加开支的某种组合。 总需求水平低和失业率高,往往会降低个人收入和公司利润,这种影响将自动减少应缴税额。失业率上升和经济较弱应导致政府在失业福利、福利和其他类似国内方案方面的支出增加。2009年,一揽子刺激措施包括延长领取失业保险的时间。 此外,自动稳定器对总需求的削弱与扩张性财政政策作出反应,并对总需求的加强与收缩性财政政策作出反应,正如反倾销和AS分析所显示的那样。

p216.original: A combination of automatic stabilizers and discretionary fiscal policy produced the very large budget deficit in 2020. The pandemic caused high levels of unemployment, meaning less tax-generating economic activity. The high unemployment rate triggered the automatic stabilizers that reduce taxes and increase spending, due to the increased amount of unemployment insurance paid out by the federal and state governments. Most economists, even those who are concerned about a possible pattern of persistently large budget deficits, are much less concerned or even quite supportive of larger budget deficits in the short run of a few years during and immediately after a severe recession.
p216.zh: 由自动稳定器和自由裁量的财政政策相结合,形成了2020年非常大的预算赤字. 这一大流行病造成高失业率,意味着产生税收的经济活动减少。 由于联邦和州政府支付失业保险金额增加,高失业率引发了减少税收和增加开支的自动稳定措施。 大多数经济学家,即使是那些担心预算赤字可能持续庞大的形态的经济学家,对在严重衰退期间和紧接着几年的短期内出现更大的预算赤字,都不太关心,甚至相当支持。

p217.original: A glance back at economic history provides a second illustration of the power of automatic stabilizers. Remember that the length of economic upswings between recessions has become longer in the U.S. economy in recent decades (as we discussed in Unemployment). The three longest economic booms of the twentieth century happened in the 1960s, the 1980s, and the 1991–2001 time period. One reason why the economy has tipped into recession less frequently in recent decades is that the size of government spending and taxes has increased in the second half of the twentieth century. Thus, the automatic stabilizing effects from spending and taxes are now larger than they were in the first half of the twentieth century. Around 1900, for example, federal spending was only about 2% of GDP. In 1929, just before the Great Depression hit, government spending was still just 4% of GDP. In those earlier times, the smaller size of government made automatic stabilizers far less powerful than in the last few decades, when government spending often hovers at 20% of GDP or more.
p217.zh: 回顾一下经济史,就可第二次说明自动稳定器的威力。记得最近几十年美国经济(正如我们在《失业》中讨论的那样)经济衰退之间的经济上升时间已经更长。二十世纪三个最长的经济繁荣时期发生在1960年代,1980年代和1991-2001年期间.经济在近几十年中不太频繁地陷入衰退的原因之一是,20世纪下半叶政府开支和税收的规模有所增加。 因此,支出和税收的自动稳定效应现在比二十世纪上半叶更大。 例如,在1900年左右,联邦开支只占国内生产总值的2%左右。1929年,就在大萧条冲击之前,政府开支仍然只占国内生产总值的4%。 在早期,政府规模较小,使得自动稳定器的威力远低于过去几十年,当时政府开支经常徘徊在GDP的20%或更多。

p218.original: The Standardized Employment Deficit or Surplus

p219.original: Each year, the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office (CBO) calculates the standardized employment budget—that is, what the budget deficit or surplus would be if the economy were producing at potential GDP, where people who look for work were finding jobs in a reasonable period of time and businesses were making normal profits, with the result that both workers and businesses would be earning more and paying more taxes. In effect, the standardized employment deficit eliminates the impact of the automatic stabilizers.  compares the actual budget deficits of recent decades with the CBO’s standardized deficit.
p219.zh: 每年,无党派的国会预算办公室(CBO)计算标准化的就业预算,即如果经济以潜在的国内生产总值生产,那么预算赤字或盈余会是什么,在那里寻找工作的人在一段合理的时间内找到工作,企业正在获得正常的利润,结果工人和企业都将获得更多的收入并支付更多的税收。 事实上,标准化的就业赤字消除了自动稳定器的影响。 将近几十年来的实际预算赤字与社区组织的标准化赤字相比较。

p220.original: Visit this website to learn more from the Congressional Budget Office.
p220.zh: 访问该网站,向国会预算办公室了解更多情况。

p221.original: Comparison of Actual Budget Deficits with the Standardized Employment Deficit
p221.zh: 实际预算赤字与标准就业赤字的比较

p222.original: Notice that in recession years, like the early 1990s, 2001, or 2009, the standardized employment deficit is smaller than the actual deficit. (These data are only available up until February 2020, so they do not include the effects of the pandemic.) During recessions, the automatic stabilizers tend to increase the budget deficit, so if the economy was instead at full employment, the deficit would be reduced. However, in the late 1990s the standardized employment budget surplus was lower than the actual budget surplus. The gap between the standardized budget deficit or surplus and the actual budget deficit or surplus shows the impact of the automatic stabilizers. More generally, the standardized budget figures allow you to see what the budget deficit would look like with the economy held constant—at its potential GDP level of output.
p222.zh: 注意到在衰退年代,如1990年代初、2001年或2009年,标准化就业赤字比实际赤字小。(这些数据直到2020年2月才提供,因此不包括该流行病的影响。 )在经济衰退期间,自动稳定因素往往会增加预算赤字,因此如果经济处于充分就业状态,赤字就会减少。 然而,在1990年代后期,标准化就业预算盈余低于实际预算盈余。标准化预算赤字或盈余与实际预算赤字或盈余之间的差距表明自动稳定器的影响。更一般地说,标准化预算数字使你可以看到预算赤字与经济维持在国内生产总值潜在产出水平上将是什么样子。

p223.original: Automatic stabilizers occur quickly. Lower wages means that a lower amount of taxes is withheld from paychecks right away. Higher unemployment or poverty means that government spending in those areas rises as quickly as people apply for benefits. However, while the automatic stabilizers offset part of the shifts in aggregate demand, they do not offset all or even most of it. Historically, automatic stabilizers on the tax and spending side offset about 10% of any initial movement in the level of output. This offset may not seem enormous, but it is still useful. Automatic stabilizers, like shock absorbers in a car, can be useful if they reduce the impact of the worst bumps, even if they do not eliminate the bumps altogether.
p223.zh: 自动稳定器迅速出现.工资较低意味着立即扣缴工资的税款较低。失业率或贫穷率上升意味着政府在这些领域的支出随着人们申请福利而迅速增加。 然而,虽然自动稳定器抵消了总需求的部分变化,但并不能抵消全部甚至大部分变化。历史上,税收和开支方面的自动稳定器抵消了产出水平的任何初始变动的10%左右。 这一抵消似乎并不巨大,但仍然有用。自动稳定器与汽车中的冲击吸收器一样,如果能够减轻最坏的冲击波的影响,即使它们不能完全消除冲击波,也可以起到作用.

p225.original: One new form of government spending meant to support working families is an expanded Child Tax Credit (CTC). Under changes which took effect in 2021, qualifying families will receive the credit as a monthly payment directly into their bank accounts. The credit is also an expanded amount: from $2,000 per child to $3,600 per child under the age of 6 (less for children older than that). Introduced by President Joe Biden’s American Rescue Plan, it is hoped that the newly expanded CTC will help reduce child poverty and support families. Because the CTC works like a grant that is automatically extended to households, the CTC is considered a new kind of fiscal policy that is related to a universal basic income policy which some have argued for in the past. By sending money out monthly instead of a lump sum as part of a person’s tax refund, the intention is to help families better manage monthly bills for things like clothes and food.
p225.zh: 旨在支持工作家庭的政府支出的一种新形式是扩大儿童税收抵免。 在2021年生效的修改中,符合条件的家庭将获得贷款,作为每月付款直接存入其银行账户。信贷数额也有所增加:从每名儿童2,000美元增加到每6岁以下儿童3,600美元(低于6岁的儿童)。由乔·拜登总统的美国拯救计划提出,希望新扩大的反恐委员会将帮助减少儿童贫穷和支持家庭。 由于反恐委员会的工作就像自动提供给家庭的赠款一样,因此反恐委员会被认为是一种新型财政政策,它与一些人过去主张的普遍基本收入政策有关。 通过每月发钱而不是一次性退还个人的税款,目的是帮助家庭更好地管理月费,如衣服和食物。

p227.original: Fiscal policy is conducted both through discretionary fiscal policy, which occurs when the government enacts taxation or spending changes in response to economic events, or through automatic stabilizers, which are taxing and spending mechanisms that, by their design, shift in response to economic events without any further legislation. The standardized employment budget is the calculation of what the budget deficit or budget surplus would have been in a given year if the economy had been producing at its potential GDP in that year. Many economists and politicians criticize the use of fiscal policy for a variety of reasons, including concerns over time lags, the impact on interest rates, and the inherently political nature of fiscal policy. We cover the critique of fiscal policy in the next module.
p227.zh: 财政政策既通过自由裁量的财政政策实施,当政府针对经济事件颁布税收或支出变化时,又通过自动稳定机制实施,这些机制是征税和支出机制,根据设计,在没有任何进一步立法的情况下,因经济事件而转变。标准化就业预算是计算如果经济在该年产生其潜在的国内生产总值,那么预算赤字或预算盈余在某一年会有多大。 许多经济学家和政治家批评财政政策的运用有多种原因,包括时间滞后的担忧,对利率的影响,以及财政政策的内在政治性质. 我们在下一个单元中谈到对财政政策的批评。

p229.original: In a recession, does the actual budget surplus or deficit fall above or below the standardized employment budget?
p229.zh: 在衰退中,实际预算盈余或赤字是否高于或低于标准化就业预算?

p230.original: It falls below because less tax revenue than expected is collected.
p230.zh: 收入低于预期的原因是税收低于预期。

p231.original: What is the main advantage of automatic stabilizers over discretionary fiscal policy?
p231.zh: 自动稳定器相对于自行酌定的财政政策的主要优势是什么?

p232.original: Automatic stabilizers take effect very quickly, whereas discretionary policy can take a long time to implement.
p232.zh: 自动稳定器迅速生效,而酌情决定的政策需要很长时间才能实施。

p233.original: Explain how automatic stabilizers work, both on the taxation side and on the spending side, first in a situation where the economy is producing less than potential GDP and then in a situation where the economy is producing more than potential GDP.
p233.zh: 解释自动稳定器如何在税收和支出方面运作,首先在经济生产低于潜在国内生产总值的情况下,然后在经济生产超过潜在国内生产总值的情况下。

p234.original: In a recession, because of the decline in economic output, less income is earned, and so less in taxes is automatically collected. Many welfare and unemployment programs are designed so that those who fall into certain categories, like “unemployed” or “low income,” are eligible for benefits. During a recession, more people fall into these categories and become eligible for benefits automatically. The combination of reduced taxes and higher spending is just what is needed for an economy in recession producing below potential GDP. With an economic boom, average income levels rise in the economy, so more in taxes is automatically collected. Fewer people meet the criteria for receiving government assistance to the unemployed or the needy, so government spending on unemployment assistance and welfare falls automatically. This combination of higher taxes and lower spending is just what is needed if an economy is producing above its potential GDP.
p234.zh: 在经济衰退中,由于经济产出下降,收入减少,因此税收减少是自动征收的. 许多福利和失业方案的设计是为了使属于某些类别的人,如“失业”或“低收入”的人有资格享受福利。 在经济衰退期间,更多的人属于这些类别,并自动获得福利。减税和增加开支的结合,正是衰退中生产低于潜在国内生产总值的经济所需要的。 随着经济的繁荣,经济中的平均收入水平上升,因此税收的更多是自动征收的.符合政府向失业者或穷人提供援助标准的人较少,因此政府在失业援助和福利方面的开支自动下降。 如果一个经济体的产量超过其潜在的国内生产总值,那么,税收增加和支出减少的这种结合就是需要的。

p236.original: What is the difference between discretionary fiscal policy and automatic stabilizers?
p236.zh: 自由裁量的财政政策和自动稳定因素之间有什么区别?

p237.zh: 为什么自动稳定器“自动”运作?

p238.original: What is the standardized employment budget?
p238.zh: 标准化就业预算是什么?

p240.original: Is Medicaid (federal government aid to low-income families and individuals) an automatic stabilizer?
p240.zh: 医疗援助(联邦政府对低收入家庭和个人的援助)是否是一种自动稳定剂?

p241.original: Practical Problems with Discretionary Fiscal Policy
p241.zh: 财政政策自由裁量的实际问题

p242.original: In the early 1960s, many leading economists believed that the problem of the business cycle, and the swings between cyclical unemployment and inflation, were a thing of the past. On the cover of its December 31, 1965, issue, Time magazine, then the premier news magazine in the United States, ran a picture of John Maynard Keynes, and the story inside identified Keynesian theories as “the prime influence on the world’s economies.” The article reported that policymakers have “used Keynesian principles not only to avoid the violent [business] cycles of prewar days but to produce phenomenal economic growth and to achieve remarkably stable prices.”
p242.zh: 1960年代初,许多主要经济学家认为,商业周期的问题,以及周期性失业和通货膨胀之间的波动,是过去的事情. 在1965年12月31日的封面上,时任美国第一任新闻杂志《时代》刊登了约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯的一幅照片,而内部的故事将凯恩斯理论确定为“对世界经济的主要影响 ” 。 文章报告说,决策者运用凯恩斯主义原则不仅是为了避免战前的暴力(商业)周期,也是为了产生惊人的经济增长并实现非常稳定的价格。

p243.original: This happy consensus, however, did not last. The U.S. economy suffered one recession from December 1969 to November 1970, a deeper recession from November 1973 to March 1975, and then double-dip recessions from January to June 1980 and from July 1981 to November 1982. At various times, inflation and unemployment both soared. Clearly, the problems of macroeconomic policy had not been completely solved. As economists began to consider what had gone wrong, they identified a number of issues that make discretionary fiscal policy more difficult than it had seemed in the rosy optimism of the mid-1960s.
p243.zh: 然而,这一愉快的共识并没有持久。1969年12月至1970年11月,美国经济经历了一次衰退,1973年11月至1975年3月更深的衰退,1980年1月至6月和1981年7月至1982年11月又经历了两次衰退.在不同时期,通货膨胀和失业都急剧上升。 显然,宏观经济政策的问题还没有完全解决。 随着经济学家开始考虑出错的原因,他们找出了一些问题,使自由裁量的财政政策比1960年代中期的乐观主义看起来更加困难。

p245.original: Because fiscal policy affects the quantity that the government borrows in financial capital markets, it not only affects aggregate demand—it can also affect interest rates. In , the original equilibrium (E0) in the financial capital market occurs at a quantity of $800 billion and an interest rate of 6%. However, an increase in government budget deficits shifts the demand for financial capital from D0 to D1. The new equilibrium (E1) occurs at a quantity of $900 billion and an interest rate of 7%.
p245.zh: 由于财政政策影响政府在金融资本市场的借款数量,它不仅影响总需求,而且还影响利率。 在......中,金融资本市场最初的平衡(E0)以8000亿美元的数量出现,利率为6%. 然而,政府预算赤字增加,对金融资本的需求从D0转向D1。 新平衡(E1)以9 000亿美元的数量出现,利率为7%。

p246.original: A consensus estimate based on a number of studies is that an increase in budget deficits (or a fall in budget surplus) by 1% of GDP will cause an increase of 0.5–1.0% in the long-term interest rate.
p246.zh: 基于一些研究的共识估计是,预算赤字增加(或预算盈余减少)占国内生产总值的1%将导致长期利率增加0.5-1.0%。

p248.original: A problem arises here. An expansionary fiscal policy, with tax cuts or spending increases, is intended to increase aggregate demand. If an expansionary fiscal policy also causes higher interest rates, then firms and households are discouraged from borrowing and spending (as occurs with tight monetary policy), thus reducing aggregate demand. Even if the direct effect of expansionary fiscal policy on increasing demand is not totally offset by lower aggregate demand from higher interest rates, fiscal policy can end up less powerful than was originally expected. We refer to this as crowding out, where government borrowing and spending results in higher interest rates, which reduces business investment and household consumption.
p248.zh: 这里出现了一个问题。扩大财政政策,减税或增加支出,意在增加总需求。 如果扩张性财政政策也导致利率上升,那么公司和家庭就不敢借贷和支出(如货币政策紧缩那样),从而减少总需求。 即使扩张性财政政策对需求增长的直接影响没有完全被利率上升导致的总体需求下降所抵消,财政政策最终可能不如原先预期的那么强大. 我们将此称为排挤,政府借贷和支出导致利率提高,从而减少了企业投资和家庭消费。

p249.original: The broader lesson is that the government must coordinate fiscal and monetary policy. If expansionary fiscal policy is to work well, then the central bank can also reduce or keep short-term interest rates low. Conversely, monetary policy can also help to ensure that contractionary fiscal policy does not lead to a recession.
p249.zh: 更广泛的教训是,政府必须协调财政和货币政策。 如果扩张性财政政策要发挥良好作用,那么中央银行也可以降低或保持短期利率的低水平. 相反,货币政策也有助于确保收缩性财政政策不会导致衰退。

p251.original: The government can change monetary policy several times each year, but it takes much longer to enact fiscal policy. Imagine that the economy starts to slow down. It often takes some months before the economic statistics signal clearly that a downturn has started, and a few months more to confirm that it is truly a recession and not just a one- or two-month blip. Economists often call the time it takes to determine that a recession has occurred the recognition lag. After this lag, policymakers become aware of the problem and propose fiscal policy bills. The bills go into various congressional committees for hearings, negotiations, votes, and then, if passed, eventually for the president’s signature. Many fiscal policy bills about spending or taxes propose changes that would start in the next budget year or would be phased in gradually over time. Economists often refer to the time it takes to pass a bill as the legislative lag. Finally, once the government passes the bill it takes some time to disperse the funds to the appropriate agencies to implement the programs. Economists call the time it takes to start the projects the implementation lag.
p251.zh: 政府每年可以改变货币政策几次,但颁布财政政策需要更长的时间.想象一下经济开始放缓.经济统计往往需要几个月的时间才能明确表明经济下滑已经开始,还需要几个月的时间才能证实,这确实是一种衰退,而不仅仅是一两个月的衰退。经济学家经常称确定衰退是否发生需要的时间为承认滞后. 在此滞后之后,决策者开始意识到这一问题,并提出了财政政策法案。法案会进入国会各个委员会进行听证、谈判、投票,如果通过,最终由总统签署。 许多关于支出或税收的财政政策法案都提出了将在下一预算年度开始或逐步分阶段进行的修改。经济学家经常将通过法案的时间称为立法滞后. 最后,一旦政府通过法案,就需要一些时间将资金分散到适当的机构来执行方案。经济学家称项目启动所需时间是执行滞后。

p252.original: Moreover, the exact level of fiscal policy that the government should implement is never completely clear. Should it increase the budget deficit by 0.5% of GDP? By 1% of GDP? By 2% of GDP? In an AD/AS diagram, it is straightforward to sketch an aggregate demand curve shifting to the potential GDP level of output. In the real world, we only know roughly, not precisely, the actual level of potential output, and exactly how a spending cut or tax increase will affect aggregate demand is always somewhat controversial. Also unknown is the state of the economy at any point in time. During the early days of the Obama administration, for example, no one knew the true extent of the economy's deficit. During the 2008-2009 financial crisis, the rapid collapse of the banking system and automotive sector made it difficult to assess how quickly the economy was collapsing.
p252.zh: 此外,政府应该执行的财政政策的确切水平也从未完全清楚。预算赤字应增加国内生产总值的0.5%吗?占国内生产总值的1%?占GDP的2%吗? 在AD/AS图中,直接勾画出总需求曲线,转向潜在的国内生产总值产出水平。 在现实世界中,我们只大致知道,而不是确切知道潜在产出的实际水平,而削减开支或增加税收究竟会如何影响总需求总是有些争议。任何时刻的经济状况也不为人所知。 例如奥巴马政府执政初期,没有人知道经济赤字的真实程度. 在2008-2009年金融危机期间,银行系统和汽车部门的迅速崩溃,使得难以评估经济崩溃的速度。

p253.original: Thus, it can take many months or even more than a year to begin an expansionary fiscal policy after a recession has started—and even then, uncertainty will remain over exactly how much to expand or contract taxes and spending. When politicians attempt to use countercyclical fiscal policy to fight recession or inflation, they run the risk of responding to the macroeconomic situation of two or three years ago, in a way that may be exactly wrong for the economy at that time. George P. Schultz, a professor of economics, former Secretary of the Treasury, and Director of the Office of Management and Budget, once wrote: “While the economist is accustomed to the concept of lags, the politician likes instant results. The tension comes because, as I have seen on many occasions, the economist’s lag is the politician’s nightmare.”
p253.zh: 因此,在衰退开始后,开始扩张性财政政策可能需要许多月甚至一年多的时间,即便如此,在扩大或收缩税收和开支的确切数量方面,不确定性仍将存在。 当政治家试图利用反周期财政政策来对抗衰退或通货膨胀时,他们就冒着对两三年前的宏观经济形势作出反应的风险,其方式可能对当时的经济完全是错误的.乔治·P.经济学教授、前财政部长兼管理和预算办公室主任舒尔茨曾写道:“经济学家虽然习惯于滞后的概念,但政治家喜欢即时结果。 我曾多次看到, 经济学家的落后是政治家的噩梦。

p255.original: A temporary tax cut or spending increase will explicitly last only for a year or two, and then revert to its original level. A permanent tax cut or spending increase is expected to stay in place for the foreseeable future. The effect of temporary and permanent fiscal policies on aggregate demand can be very different. Consider how you would react if the government announced a tax cut that would last one year and then be repealed, in comparison with how you would react if the government announced a permanent tax cut. Most people and firms will react more strongly to a permanent policy change than a temporary one.
p255.zh: 临时减税或增加开支将明确持续一年或两年,然后恢复到原来的水平。 预计在可预见的将来将长期减少税收或增加开支。临时和长期财政政策对总需求的影响可能大不相同。想想如果政府宣布减税一年,然后取消, 与政府宣布永久减税时你的反应相比,大多数人和公司对永久政策变化的反应比暂时的更强烈。

p256.original: This fact creates an unavoidable difficulty for countercyclical fiscal policy. The appropriate policy may be to have an expansionary fiscal policy with large budget deficits during a recession, and then a contractionary fiscal policy with budget surpluses when the economy is growing well. However, if both policies are explicitly temporary ones, they will have a less powerful effect than a permanent policy.
p256.zh: 这一事实给反周期性财政政策造成了不可避免的困难。适当的政策可能是,在经济衰退期间,实行具有庞大预算赤字的扩张性财政政策,然后在经济增长良好时实行具有预算盈余的紧缩性财政政策。 然而,如果两种政策都明确属于临时性政策,那么它们的效果将不如永久性政策大。

p257.zh: 结构经济变革需要时间

p258.original: When an economy recovers from a recession, it does not usually revert to its exact earlier shape. Instead, the economy's internal structure evolves and changes and this process can take time. For example, much of the economic growth of the mid-2000s was in the construction sector (especially of housing) and finance. However, when housing prices started falling in 2007 and the resulting financial crunch led into recession (as we discussed in Monetary Policy and Bank Regulation), both sectors contracted. The manufacturing sector of the U.S. economy has been losing jobs in recent years as well, under pressure from technological change and foreign competition. Many of the people who lost work from these sectors in the 2008-2009 Great Recession will never return to the same jobs in the same sectors of the economy. Instead, the economy will need to grow in new and different directions, as the following Clear It Up feature shows. Fiscal policy can increase overall demand, but the process of structural economic change—the expansion of a new set of industries and the movement of workers to those industries—inevitably takes time.
p258.zh: 当一个经济体从衰退中复苏时,通常不会恢复到其先前的形状。 相反,经济的内部结构正在演变和变化,这一过程可能需要时间。 例如,2000年代中期的经济增长大多在建筑部门(特别是住房)和金融领域。 然而,当2007年住房价格开始下跌,由此产生的金融紧缩导致衰退(正如我们在货币政策和银行监管中所讨论的那样)时,这两个部门都收缩了。 近年来,美国经济的制造业部门也在技术变革和外国竞争的压力下失去了工作。 在2008-2009年大衰退中失去这些部门工作的许多人永远不会回到同一经济部门的相同工作。 相反,经济需要以新的和不同的方向发展,正如下面的Clear It Up 特征所显示的那样。财政政策可以增加总体需求,但结构经济变革的进程——扩大新产业和工人向这些产业流动——需要时间,这是不可避免的。

p260.original: People can lose jobs for a variety of reasons: because of a recession, but also because of longer-run changes in the economy, such as new technology. Productivity improvements in auto manufacturing, for example, can reduce the number of workers needed, and eliminate these jobs in the long run. The internet has created jobs but also caused job loss, from travel agents to book store clerks. Many of these jobs may never come back. Short-run fiscal policy to reduce unemployment can create jobs, but it cannot replace jobs that will never return.
p260.zh: 人们可能因为各种原因失去工作:因为经济衰退,但也因为经济的较长期变化,如新技术. 例如,提高汽车制造业的生产力可以减少所需工人人数,并从长远来看消除这些工作。互联网创造了工作机会,但也造成了从旅行社到书店职员的失业。其中许多工作可能永远也不会回来。减少失业的短期财政政策可以创造就业机会,但不能取代永远不会返回的工作。

p262.original: Fiscal policy can help an economy that is producing below its potential GDP to expand aggregate demand so that it produces closer to potential GDP, thus lowering unemployment. However, fiscal policy cannot help an economy produce at an output level above potential GDP without causing inflation At this point, unemployment becomes so low that workers become scarce and wages rise rapidly.
p262.zh: 财政政策可以帮助一个生产低于其潜在国内总产值的经济扩大总需求,使其生产更接近潜在国内总产值,从而降低失业率。 然而,财政政策不能帮助一个经济体在产出水平上高于潜在国内生产总值,而不会造成通货膨胀。

p263.original: Visit  this website to read about how fiscal policies are affecting the recovery.
p263.zh: 访问该网站,了解财政政策如何影响复苏。

p264.original: Political Realties and Discretionary Fiscal Policy
p264.zh: 政治现实和审慎的财政政策

p265.original: A final problem for discretionary fiscal policy arises out of the difficulties of explaining to politicians how countercyclical fiscal policy that runs against the tide of the business cycle should work. Some politicians have a gut-level belief that when the economy and tax revenues slow down, it is time to hunker down, pinch pennies, and trim expenses. Countercyclical policy, however, says that when the economy has slowed, it is time for the government to stimulate the economy, raising spending, and cutting taxes. This offsets the drop in the economy in the other sectors. Conversely, when economic times are good and tax revenues are rolling in, politicians often feel that it is time for tax cuts and new spending. However, countercyclical policy says that this economic boom should be an appropriate time for keeping taxes high and restraining spending.
p265.zh: 自由裁量的财政政策的最后问题在于难以向政治家解释反周期的财政政策如何应对商业周期的潮流。 一些政客有直觉的信念,当经济和税收减速时,是时候去打压、扣钱和削减开支了。 但反周期政策说,当经济放缓时,政府应该刺激经济,增加开支,削减税收. 这抵消了其他部门经济的下降。 相反,当经济时代好,税收不断滚动时,政治家们往往认为现在是减税和新支出的时候了。 然而,反周期政策说,这种经济繁荣应当是保持高税收和限制开支的适当时机。

p266.original: Politicians tend to prefer expansionary fiscal policy over contractionary policy. There is rarely a shortage of proposals for tax cuts and spending increases, especially during recessions. However, politicians are less willing to hear the message that in good economic times, they should propose tax increases and spending limits. In the economic upswing of the late 1990s and early 2000s, for example, the U.S. GDP grew rapidly. Estimates from respected government economic forecasters like the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office and the Office of Management and Budget stated that the GDP was above potential GDP, and that unemployment rates were unsustainably low. However, no mainstream politician took the lead in saying that the booming economic times might be an appropriate time for spending cuts or tax increases.
p266.zh: 政治家倾向于扩张性的财政政策而不是收缩性政策.减税和增加开支的建议很少,特别是在经济衰退期间。 然而,政治家们不太愿意听到这样的信息:在良好的经济时期,他们应该提出增税和支出限制. 例如,在1990年代末和2000年代初期的经济增长中,美国。国内生产总值增长迅速。 来自无党派国会预算办公室以及管理和预算办公室等受人尊敬的政府经济预测者的估计表明,国内生产总值高于潜在国内生产总值,失业率低得难以维持。 然而,没有主流政治人物带头说,繁荣的经济时代可能是削减开支或增加税收的适当时机。

p268.original: Expansionary fiscal policy can help to end recessions and contractionary fiscal policy can help to reduce inflation. Given the uncertainties over interest rate effects, time lags, temporary and permanent policies, and unpredictable political behavior, many economists and knowledgeable policymakers had concluded by the mid-1990s that discretionary fiscal policy was a blunt instrument, more like a club than a scalpel. It might still make sense to use it in extreme economic situations, like an especially deep or long recession. For less extreme situations, it was often preferable to let fiscal policy work through the automatic stabilizers and focus on monetary policy to steer short-term countercyclical efforts.
p268.zh: 扩张性财政政策可以帮助结束衰退,收缩性财政政策可以帮助降低通货膨胀. 鉴于利率效应、时间滞后、临时和永久政策以及不可预测的政治行为等不确定性,许多经济学家和有知识的决策者到1990年代中期得出结论,酌情制定的财政政策是一种钝器,更像是俱乐部而不是手术刀。 在极端的经济状况下使用它可能仍然有意义,比如特别深或长期的衰退。 对于不太极端的情况,往往最好是让财政政策通过自动稳定器发挥作用,并注重货币政策,以指导短期反周期努力。

p270.original: Because fiscal policy affects the quantity of money that the government borrows in financial capital markets, it not only affects aggregate demand—it can also affect interest rates. If an expansionary fiscal policy also causes higher interest rates, then firms and households are discouraged from borrowing and spending, reducing aggregate demand in a situation called crowding out. Given the uncertainties over interest rate effects, time lags (implementation lag, legislative lag, and recognition lag), temporary and permanent policies, and unpredictable political behavior, many economists and knowledgeable policymakers have concluded that discretionary fiscal policy is a blunt instrument and better used only in extreme situations.
p270.zh: 由于财政政策影响政府在金融资本市场上借入的资金数量,它不仅影响总需求,而且还影响利率。 如果扩张性财政政策也导致利率上升,那么公司和家庭就不敢借贷和支出,在所谓挤出的情况下减少总需求。 鉴于利率效应的不确定性、时间滞后(执行滞后、立法滞后和承认滞后)、临时和永久政策以及不可预测的政治行为,许多经济学家和有知识的决策者得出结论,酌情的财政政策是一种钝器,只在极端情况下才得到更好的使用。

p272.original: What would happen if expansionary fiscal policy was implemented in a recession but, due to lag, did not actually take effect until after the economy was back to potential GDP?
p272.zh: 如果在衰退中实施扩张性财政政策,但由于滞后,在经济恢复到潜在的国内生产总值之后,政策才实际生效,那么会发生什么?

p273.original: Prices would be pushed up as a result of too much spending.
p273.zh: 由于支出过多,价格会上涨。

p274.original: What would happen if contractionary fiscal policy were implemented during an economic boom but, due to lag, it did not take effect until the economy slipped into recession?
p274.zh: 如果在经济繁荣期间执行收缩性财政政策,但由于滞后,在经济滑入衰退之前,政策不会生效,那么会怎样呢?

p275.original: Employment would suffer as a result of too little spending.
p275.zh: 由于开支太少,就业将受到影响。

p276.original: Do you think the typical time lag for fiscal policy is likely to be longer or shorter than the time lag for monetary policy? Explain your answer?
p276.zh: 你认为财政政策的典型滞后时间可能比货币政策的滞后时间长或短吗?解释你的答案?

p277.original: Monetary policy probably has shorter time lags than fiscal policy. Imagine that the data becomes fairly clear that an economy is in or near a recession. Expansionary monetary policy can be carried out through open market operations, which can be done fairly quickly, since the Federal Reserve’s Open Market Committee meets six times a year. Also, monetary policy takes effect through interest rates, which can change fairly quickly. However, fiscal policy is carried out through acts of Congress that need to be signed into law by the president. Negotiating such laws often takes months, and even after the laws are negotiated, it takes more months for spending programs or tax cuts to have an effect on the macroeconomy.
p277.zh: 货币政策的滞后时间可能比财政政策短。想象一下,数据变得相当清楚,一个经济体正在或接近衰退。扩张性货币政策可以通过开放市场来实施,而开放市场可以相当迅速地实施,因为美联储的开放市场委员会每年召开六次会议。 此外,货币政策通过利率生效,利率可以相当迅速地变化。 然而,财政政策是通过需要总统签署成为法律的国会法案来执行的.谈判这类法律往往需要几个月时间,即使在谈判法律之后,支出方案或减税也需要更多月的时间才能对宏观经济产生影响。

p279.original: What are some practical weaknesses of discretionary fiscal policy?
p279.zh: 自由裁量的财政政策有哪些实际弱点?

p281.original: What is a potential problem with a temporary tax decrease designed to increase aggregate demand if people know that it is temporary?
p281.zh: 如果人们知道是暂时的,那么旨在增加总需求的临时减税的潜在问题是什么?

p282.original: If the government gives a $300 tax cut to everyone in the country, explain the mechanism by which this will cause interest rates to rise.
p282.zh: 如果政府给全国每个人300美元的减税,请解释这会导致利率上升的机制.

p288.original: The Question of a Balanced Budget

p289.original: For many decades, going back to the 1930s, various legislators have put forward proposals to require that the U.S. government balance its budget every year. In 1995, a proposed constitutional amendment that would require a balanced budget passed the U.S. House of Representatives by a wide margin, and failed in the U.S. Senate by only a single vote. (For the balanced budget to have become an amendment to the Constitution would have required a two-thirds vote by Congress and passage by three-quarters of the state legislatures.)
p289.zh: 几十年来,早在1930年代,各种立法者就提出了要求美国政府每年平衡预算的建议.1995年,一项需要平衡预算的宪法修正案提案通过了美国.众议院以大势,败于美国.参议院只以一票之差.(为使预算平衡成为《宪法》修正案,需要国会三分之二多数票和四分之三的州立法机构通过。 )

p290.original: Most economists view the proposals for a perpetually balanced budget with bemusement. After all, in the short term, economists would expect the budget deficits and surpluses to fluctuate up and down with the economy and the automatic stabilizers. Economic recessions should automatically lead to larger budget deficits or smaller budget surpluses, while economic booms lead to smaller deficits or larger surpluses. A requirement that the budget be balanced each and every year would prevent these automatic stabilizers from working and would worsen the severity of economic fluctuations.
p290.zh: 大多数经济学家都认为,预算应始终保持平衡,并要有雄心。毕竟,从短期来看,经济学家们预计预算赤字和盈余会随经济和自动稳定因素而上下波动。经济衰退应自动导致更大的预算赤字或较小的预算盈余,而经济繁荣则导致较小的赤字或较大的盈余。要求预算每年平衡,将阻止这些自动稳定器发挥作用,并加剧经济波动的严重性。

p291.original: Some supporters of the balanced budget amendment like to argue that, since households must balance their own budgets, the government should too. However, this analogy between household and government behavior is severely flawed. Most households do not balance their budgets every year. Some years households borrow to buy houses or cars or to pay for medical expenses or college tuition. Other years they repay loans and save funds in retirement accounts. After retirement, they withdraw and spend those savings. Also, the government is not a household for many reasons, one of which is that the government has macroeconomic responsibilities. The argument of Keynesian macroeconomic policy is that the government needs to lean against the wind, spending when times are hard and saving when times are good, for the sake of the overall economy.
p291.zh: 一些支持平衡预算修正案的人喜欢认为,由于家庭必须平衡自己的预算,政府也应该如此. 然而,这种家庭和政府行为的类比存在严重缺陷. 大多数家庭每年不平衡预算。几年来,一些家庭借钱购买房屋或汽车,或支付医疗费用或大学学费。 其他年份,他们还贷,并在退休账户中储蓄资金。退休后,他们退出并花掉这些积蓄。 另外,由于许多原因,政府不是家庭,其中一个原因是政府负有宏观经济责任. 凯恩斯主义宏观经济政策的论据是,政府需要靠风抗风,在困难的时候花钱,在好的时候储蓄,以利整体经济.

p292.original: There is also no particular reason to expect a government budget to be balanced in the medium term of a few years. For example, a government may decide that by running large budget deficits, it can make crucial long-term investments in human capital and physical infrastructure that will build the country's long-term productivity. These decisions may work out well or poorly, but they are not always irrational. Such policies of ongoing government budget deficits may persist for decades. As the U.S. experience from the end of World War II up to about 1980 shows, it is perfectly possible to run budget deficits almost every year for decades, but as long as the percentage increases in debt are smaller than the percentage growth of GDP, the debt/GDP ratio will decline at the same time.
p292.zh: 也没有特别理由期望在几年的中期里政府预算能够平衡。 例如,政府可能决定,如果出现巨额预算赤字,它可以对人力资本和有形基础设施进行关键的长期投资,从而建设国家的长期生产力。 这些决定可能效果良好或很差,但并不总是不合理。 政府预算赤字的这种政策可能持续几十年。 正如美国从二战结束到大约1980年的经验表明,几十年来几乎每年都有预算赤字是完全可能的,但只要债务增加的百分比小于GDP增长的百分比,债务/GDP比率就会同时下降.

p293.original: Nothing in this argument is a claim that budget deficits are always a wise policy. In the short run, a government that runs a very large budget deficit can shift aggregate demand to the right and trigger severe inflation. Additionally, governments may borrow for foolish or impractical reasons. The Impacts of Government Borrowing will discuss how large budget deficits, by reducing national saving, can in certain cases reduce economic growth and even contribute to international financial crises. A requirement that the budget be balanced in each calendar year, however, is a misguided overreaction to the fear that in some cases, budget deficits can become too large.
p293.zh: 这一论点中没有任何内容是声称预算赤字始终是明智的政策。 从短期来看,一个预算赤字非常大的政府可以将总需求转移到正确的水平,并引发严重的通货膨胀. 此外,政府可能出于愚蠢或不切实际的理由借贷。" 政府借款的影响 " 将讨论通过减少国民储蓄,在某些情况下如何减少经济增长,甚至助长国际金融危机。 然而,要求预算在每个历年保持平衡,是对在某些情况下预算赤字可能太大的担心的错误反应。

p295.original: The 2013 federal budget shutdown illustrated the many sides to fiscal policy and the federal budget. In 2013, Republicans and Democrats could not agree on which spending policies to fund and how large the government debt should be. Due to the severity of the 2008-2009 recession, the fiscal stimulus, and previous policies, the federal budget deficit and debt was historically high. One way to try to cut federal spending and borrowing was to refuse to raise the legal federal debt limit, or tie on conditions to appropriation bills to stop the Affordable Health Care Act. This disagreement led to a two-week federal government shutdown and got close to the deadline where the federal government would default on its Treasury bonds. Finally, however, a compromise emerged and the government avoided default. This shows clearly how closely fiscal policies are tied to politics.
p295.zh: 2013年的联邦预算停工表明了财政政策和联邦预算的诸多方面.2013年,共和党人和民主党人无法就哪些支出政策可以资助以及政府债务应该有多大达成一致. 由于2008-2009年衰退的严重程度、财政刺激措施以及以往的政策,联邦预算赤字和债务历来很高。试图削减联邦开支和借贷的一个方法是拒绝提高联邦法定债务限额,或者与拨款条件挂钩,以阻止"负担得起的保健法". 这一分歧导致联邦政府停业两周,并接近联邦政府拖欠国库债券的最后期限. 然而,最后出现了妥协,政府避免了违约. 这清楚地表明,财政政策与政治的关系是多么密切。

p297.original: Balanced budget amendments are a popular political idea, but the economic merits behind such proposals are questionable. Most economists accept that fiscal policy needs to be flexible enough to accommodate unforeseen expenditures, such as wars or recessions. While persistent, large budget deficits can indeed be a problem, a balanced budget amendment prevents even small, temporary deficits that might, in some cases, be necessary.
p297.zh: 预算的平衡修正是一个受欢迎的政治想法,但这种提议背后的经济优点是值得怀疑的。 大多数经济学家都认为,财政政策需要有足够的灵活性,以适应诸如战争或衰退等无法预料的开支. 尽管预算赤字居高不下,但预算赤字可能确实是一个问题,但平衡的预算修正甚至可以防止一些可能必要的小型临时赤字。

p299.original: How would a balanced budget amendment affect a decision by Congress to grant a tax cut during a recession?
p299.zh: 平衡的预算修正案将如何影响国会在经济衰退期间准予减税的决定?

p300.original: The government would have to make up the revenue either by raising taxes in a different area or cutting spending.
p300.zh: 政府必须通过在另一地区提高税收或削减开支来弥补收入。

p301.original: How would a balanced budget amendment change the effect of automatic stabilizer programs?
p301.zh: 平衡的预算修正如何改变自动稳定器方案的效果?

p302.original: Programs where the amount of spending is not fixed, but rather determined by macroeconomic conditions, such as food stamps, would lose a great deal of flexibility if spending increases had to be met by corresponding tax increases or spending cuts.
p302.zh: 支出数额没有固定,而是由宏观经济条件决定的方案,如粮票等,如果必须通过相应增税或削减支出来应付支出的增加,将失去很大的灵活性。

p304.original: What are some of the arguments for and against a requirement that the federal government budget be balanced every year?
p304.zh: 要求联邦政府预算每年实现平衡,有什么理由和反对意见?

p306.original: Do you agree or disagree with this statement: “It is in the best interest of our economy for Congress and the President to run a balanced budget each year.” Explain your answer.
p306.zh: 你是否同意或不同意这一说法:“国会和总统每年进行平衡的预算,符合我们的经济利益。”

p307.original: During the Great Recession of 2008–2009, what actions would have been required of Congress and the President had a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution been ratified? What impact would that have had on the unemployment rate?
p307.zh: 在2008-2009年的大衰退期间,如果批准对宪法的平衡预算修正案,需要国会和总统采取哪些行动?这会对失业率产生什么影响?

c0.original: Yellowstone National Park is one of the many national parks forced to close operations during the government shut down in 2013 and 2018–2019. (Credit: modification of “Close up of sign” by David Fulmer/Flickr Creative Commons, CC BY 2.0)
c0.zh: 黄石国家公园是2013年和2018–2019年政府关闭期间被迫关闭运营的众多国家公园之一.(编辑:David Fulmer/Flickr Creative Communitys, CC BY 2. 0) 修改了“签名的关闭”。

c1.original: Since 1960, total federal spending has ranged from about 18% to 22% of GDP. It climbed above that level in 2009, quickly dropped back down to that level by 2013, and again climbed above that level in 2020. The share that the government has spent on national defense has generally declined, while the share it has spent on Social Security and on healthcare expenses (mainly Medicare and Medicaid) has increased. (Source: Economic Report of the President, 2021, Table B47, https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021)
c1.zh: 自1960年以来,联邦总支出占国内生产总值的18%至22%不等。2009年攀升到该水平以上,到2013年迅速回落到该水平以上,2020年再次攀升到该水平以上.政府在国防方面花费的份额普遍下降,而在社会保障和保健费用(主要是医疗保险和医疗补助)方面花费的份额也有所增加。(资料来源:总统经济报告,2021年,表B47,https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021)

c2.original: About 60% of government spending goes to four major areas: national defense, Social Security, healthcare, and interest payments on past borrowing. This leaves about 40% of federal spending for all other functions of the U.S. government. (Source: https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/budget/Historicals/)
c2.zh: 政府支出的60%用于四个主要领域:国防、社会保障、医疗保健和过去借款利息支付。 这为美国政府所有其他职能留下了大约40%的联邦开支.(资料来源:https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/document/Historicals/).

c3.original: Spending by state and local government increased from about 10% of GDP in the early 1960s to 14–16% by the mid-1970s. It has remained at roughly that level since. The single biggest spending item is education, including both K–12 spending and support for public colleges and universities, which has been about 4–5% of GDP in recent decades. Source: (Source: Bureau of Economic Analysis, https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/index_nipa.cfm.)
c3.zh: 州和地方政府的支出从1960年代初占国内生产总值的10%左右增加到1970年代中期的14-16%。自那时以来,这一水平一直维持在大约这一水平。最大的支出项目是教育,包括K-12-12支出和对公立学院和大学的支持,近几十年来,这些开支约占GDP的4-5 % 。 资料来源:经济分析局,https://apps.bea.gov/itable/index_nipa.cfm。 )

c4.original: Federal tax revenues have been about 17–20% of GDP during most periods in recent decades. The primary sources of federal taxes are individual income taxes and the payroll taxes that finance Social Security and Medicare. Corporate income taxes and social insurance taxes provide smaller shares of revenue. (Source: Economic Report of the President, 2021. Table B-47, https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021)
c4.zh: 在最近几十年的大部分时间里,联邦的税收收入约为国内生产总值的17-20%。联邦税收的主要来源是个人所得税和为社会保障和医疗保险提供资金的工资税。公司所得税和社会保险税收入份额较小。(资料来源:2021年总统经济报告). 表B-47,https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021

c5.original: State and local tax revenues have increased to match the rise in state and local spending.  (Source: Economic Report of the President, 2020. Table B-50, https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021)
c5.zh: 国家和地方的税收有所增加,以适应州和地方支出的增长。(资料来源:2020年总统经济报告). 表B-50,https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021

c6.original: The federal government has run budget deficits for decades. The budget was briefly in surplus in the late 1990s, before heading into deficit again in the first decade of the 2000s—and especially deep deficits in the 2007-2009 and 2020 recessions. (Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED). http://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/FYFSGDA188S)
c6.zh: 联邦政府几十年来一直存在预算赤字.1990年代末期,预算短暂出现盈余,然后在2000年代的头十年再次出现赤字,在2007-2009年和2020年的衰退中赤字尤其严重。(资料来源:圣美联储银行)Louis (FRED). http://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/FYFSGDA188S).

c7.original: Federal debt is the sum of annual budget deficits and surpluses. Annual deficits do not always mean that the debt/GDP ratio is rising. During the 1960s and 1970s, the government often ran small deficits, but since the debt was growing more slowly than the economy, the debt/GDP ratio was declining over this time. In the 2008–2009 recession, the debt/GDP ratio rose sharply, before leveling off through the later 2010s. In 2020, it rose sharply again. (Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GFDEGDQ188S)
c7.zh: 联邦债务是年度预算赤字和盈余的总和.年度赤字并不总是意味着债务/国内生产总值比率在上升。1960年代和1970年代,政府经常出现小额赤字,但由于债务增长比经济慢,债务/GDP比率在这段时间内不断下降. 在2008-2009年的衰退中,债务/国内生产总值比率急剧上升,直至2010年代后期才趋于平息。2020年,再次急剧上升.(资料来源:https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GFDEGDQ188S)

c8.original: When government spending exceeds taxes, the gap is the budget deficit. When taxes exceed spending, the gap is a budget surplus. The recessionary period starting in late 2007 saw higher spending and lower taxes, combining to create a large deficit in 2009. The same thing happened in a more extreme way in 2020. (Source: Economic Report of the President, Tables B-46, https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021)
c8.zh: 当政府支出超过税收时,缺口就是预算赤字. 当税收超过支出时,缺口就是预算盈余.2007年末开始的衰退时期,支出增加,税收减少,2009年合并形成巨额赤字。2020年,同样的事情以更极端的方式发生.(资料来源:总统经济报告,表B-46,https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/erp/2021)

c9.original: In this well-functioning economy, each year aggregate supply and aggregate demand shift to the right so that the economy proceeds from equilibrium E0 to E1 to E2. Each year, the economy produces at potential GDP with only a small inflationary increase in the price level. However, if aggregate demand does not smoothly shift to the right and match increases in aggregate supply, growth with deflation can develop.
c9.zh: 在这个运作良好的经济体中,每年总供应量和总需求向右转移,使经济从E0到E1到E2的均衡发展。经济每年以潜在的国内生产总值生产,而物价水平只有小幅的通胀增长. 但是,如果总需求不能顺利向右转移,使总供应量的增长相匹配,则增长与通货紧缩可以发展起来.

c10.original: The original equilibrium (E0) represents a recession, occurring at a quantity of output (Y0) below potential GDP. However, a shift of aggregate demand from AD0 to AD1, enacted through an expansionary fiscal policy, can move the economy to a new equilibrium output of E1 at the level of potential GDP which the LRAS curve shows. Since the economy was originally producing below potential GDP, any inflationary increase in the price level from P0 to P1 that results should be relatively small.
c10.zh: 最初的平衡(E0)是衰退,其产出量(Y0)低于潜在国内生产总值。 然而,通过扩张性财政政策将总需求从AD0转向AD1,可以使经济在LIS曲线显示的潜在GDP水平上转向E1的新平衡产出。 由于经济最初的产值低于潜在的国内生产总值,因此,从P0到P1的价格水平的任何通货膨胀上升,其结果都应该相对较小。

c11.original: The economy starts at the equilibrium quantity of output Y0, which is above potential GDP. The extremely high level of aggregate demand will generate inflationary increases in the price level. A contractionary fiscal policy can shift aggregate demand down from AD0 to AD1, leading to a new equilibrium output E1, which occurs at potential GDP, where AD1 intersects the LRAS curve.
c11.zh: 经济始于产出的平衡数量Y0, 高于潜在的国内生产总值。需求总额极高,将造成物价水平的通货膨胀上升。收缩的财政政策可以将总需求从AD0转向AD1,从而形成新的平衡产出E1,这种产出发生在潜在的国内生产总值中,AD1与LISS曲线交叉。

c12.original: When the economy is in recession, the standardized employment budget deficit is less than the actual budget deficit because the economy is below potential GDP, and the automatic stabilizers are reducing taxes and increasing spending. When the economy is performing extremely well, the standardized employment deficit (or surplus) is higher than the actual budget deficit (or surplus) because the economy is producing about potential GDP, so the automatic stabilizers are increasing taxes and reducing the need for government spending. (Sources: Actual and Cyclically Adjusted Budget Surpluses/Deficits, https://www.cbo.gov/data/budget-economic-data#8)
c12.zh: 当经济陷入衰退时,标准化的就业预算赤字低于实际预算赤字,因为经济低于潜在的GDP,自动稳定器正在减少税收和增加支出. 当经济表现极佳时,标准化的就业赤字(或盈余)比实际预算赤字(或盈余)要高,因为经济正在产生潜在的GDP,所以自动稳定器正在增加税收,减少对政府支出的需求.(资料来源:实际和经循环调整的预算盈余/赤字,https://www.cbo.gov/data/economic-data#8)

c13.original: When a government borrows money in the financial capital market, it causes a shift in the demand for financial capital from D0 to D1. As the equilibrium moves from E0 to E1, the equilibrium interest rate rises from 6% to 7% in this example. In this way, an expansionary fiscal policy intended to shift aggregate demand to the right can also lead to a higher interest rate, which has the effect of shifting aggregate demand back to the left.
c13.zh: 当政府在金融资本市场上借钱时,会导致对金融资本的需求从D0转向D1. 随着平衡从E0升至E1,在此例子中,平衡利率从6%升至7%. 这样,旨在将总需求转向右侧的扩张性财政政策也会导致更高的利率,而利率的影响是将总需求向左侧转移。
